text:
Olivia C.: Hey team — after we flipped the auth host to https://auth.new-corp.example.com several customers are hitting OAuth failures. Both GitHub and Google flows sometimes end up with `invalid_state` or `invalid_grant` with an ‘Invalid PKCE verifier’ message when we POST to our token endpoint.
Repro I have: click Sign in with GitHub -> redirect to provider -> callback to https://auth.new-corp.example.com/callback?code=XXX&state=YYY -> our backend POSTs to /oauth/token -> 400 {\"error\":\"invalid_grant\",\"error_description\":\"Invalid PKCE verifier\"}.
Observed on Chrome desktop and iOS Safari. Happened right after today's auth-host deploy. trace_id in logs: tX98-abc. Any quick checks we should run?

Maria S.: thanks, Olivia. Can you paste the exact redirect_uri your app is sending during the token exchange (must match the configured callback in the provider app settings exactly, including trailing slash). Also: are we storing `state` in session cookie or localStorage? If cookie, what's SameSite?

Olivia C.: redirect_uri used is `https://auth.new-corp.example.com/callback` (no trailing slash). Our app previously used `https://auth.redwoodinfra.com/callback` — we updated provider settings but I need to double-check both GitHub & Google entries. We store state in a session cookie (HttpOnly). Cookie config from env: `SESSION_SAMESITE=Lax`, domain set to `.new-corp.example.com`.

Sandeep R.: Lax could be the culprit for certain browsers if the redirect counts as a cross-site POST. When the provider redirects back, browsers sometimes treat that as third-party context and won't send cookies with SameSite=Lax in some flows, which means the server doesn't see the original state. That would surface as `invalid_state` on our side. Also check that our reverse proxy isn't normalizing the query string (some proxies strip `state` if they think it's a duplicate param).

Jason K.: quick troubleshooting checklist: 1) Compare `state` returned in callback query vs `state` stored in session for that trace_id (tX98-abc). 2) Capture the POST payload sent from backend to token endpoint — specifically `code_verifier`. 3) Try a direct token exchange from CLI to rule out our backend lib. Example curl:```\ncurl -X POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token \\n  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \\n  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \\n  -d code=THE_CODE_FROM_CALLBACK \\n  -d redirect_uri=https://auth.new-corp.example.com/callback \\n  -d code_verifier=THE_CODE_VERIFIER_FROM_PKCE
```\nIf that succeeds, it's our server-layer losing or mangling `code_verifier` / `redirect_uri` during the exchange.

Maria S.: also check PKCE method: are we sending `code_challenge_method=S256`? If the provider expects S256 but the client generated plain it will fail verification. GitHub + Google both accept S256; many libs use it by default but double-check.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T09:22:13Z completed: auth-service @ canary -> prod. Env change: OAUTH_REDIRECT_HOST=auth.new-corp.example.com (previously auth.redwoodinfra.com)

Olivia C.: did a quick raw check: I captured the callback and compared the state. The `state` query param coming back (YYY) matches the value we set, but our server session lookup fails because the session cookie is not present on the callback request (checked with tcpdump on the pod). Cookie indeed not sent to auth.new-corp.example.com on that request.

Sandeep R.: that nails it — cookie missing -> server has no stored code_verifier/state -> PKCE/state mismatch. Two immediate fixes: 1) Change SESSION_SAMESITE=None; Secure for the cookie (then browsers will send it on cross-site redirects), OR 2) switch to storing state in the redirect URL (less ideal). We should also confirm our cookie domain (leading dot) matches the host.

Maria S.: for mitigation: can you ask the customer to try an incognito window or Chrome desktop and send back network trace? Also check provider app settings for the exact redirect URI string — if provider rejects a token exchange because `redirect_uri` differs slightly that will also manifest. But given the tcpdump, cookie is missing so fix cookie attrs first.

Olivia C.: trying SESSION_SAMESITE=None locally by overriding env and restarting auth pods now. Will report back in a few mins. Thanks. :pray:

Olivia C. (later): quick update — after we set SESSION_SAMESITE=None and redeployed, two users confirmed GitHub + Google login succeeded. Leaving this here in case anyone hits similar after host changes: cookie SameSite is a common silent failure. Also watch out for provider app redirect_uri exactness and trailing-slash normalization by proxies.

Sandeep R.: thanks — follow-up items: (a) make SESSION_SAMESITE=None the default for auth-service and add a changelog note, (b) run a small canary to ensure no CSRF regressions, (c) add telemetry when `state` cookie missing to make debugging easier. I'll open a quick PR.

Maria S.: I'll reply to the customer with the root cause and workaround. Closing the thread once we have the PR link. :white_check_mark:
